`forks.jsonl` contains 430 graphs generated by
`python3 tools/generate_fork_fixtures.py --source ../mmx-node`, against reference
commit `ca6438b37c08007106d58efe4a990f6ecb276649`.

The generator extracts `Node::find_best_fork` verbatim, changing only its class
qualifier. A minimal harness supplies the native fork fields, weak parent links,
height multimap, header lookup, root and pending sync heights. Native MMX/VNX
types provide uint128 arithmetic and raw hash ordering. Expected results include
the chosen hash and every active fork's propagated root, cumulative uint32 votes,
invalid flag and all-proofs-verified flag.

Cases cover lighter/heavier peaks and roots, votes taking precedence at equal
root weight, wrapping cumulative votes, height and raw-byte hash ties,
unverified/invalid/missing parents, missing anchors, backwards-sync guards and
400 reproducible randomized graphs. Candidate order is arrival order; the native
multimap supplies stable height ordering. Votes and proof flags are trusted
inputs to this policy oracle, independently of vote/proof authentication.

Ordinary Rust tests use these checked-in results without a C++ build.
